resources.string: TextGate AI reads ONLY the text field you are currently editing, and only to look for the exact suffix \"?en\" or \"?pl\" at the end of what you\'ve typed. It never reads password fields, never reads other apps\' content, never runs in apps you have not explicitly allowed, and never keeps a history of anything you type. When \"?en\" or \"?pl\" is detected in an allowed app, the text before it is sent over HTTPS to the Gemini API you have configured, translated into English or Polish respectively, and used to replace the field\'s contents. Nothing is sent anywhere unless you type one of these exact triggers in an app that is switched on in TextGate AI\'s settings.

Master switch. Type ?en at the end of a message to translate it to English, or ?pl to translate it to Polish. When off, TextGate AI never reads any field and never makes any network request, regardless of any other setting below.
Not enabled — TextGate AI cannot do anything until you enable it
API key saved, encrypted with Android Keystore
A key is saved (encrypted). It is never shown again on screen.

TextGate AI is enabled by default for common social media and messaging apps only — for example WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, Telegram, Signal, Discord, Snapchat, TikTok, X, Threads, LinkedIn, and SMS/Messages — so there is nothing to set up. Known password managers, banking, authenticator, and system security apps are never shown here and can never be enabled; cryptocurrency wallets and exchanges are blocked the same way.
Want a different app, or to remove one of the defaults? Choose apps by hand instead.
No apps installed with a launcher icon were found.
Text is sent to Google Gemini only when you explicitly use the ?en or ?pl trigger.

TextGate AI does not collect analytics, crash reports, or usage data of any kind, and contains no third-party SDKs. The only network requests this app ever makes are the translation requests you trigger yourself, sent directly to Google\'s Gemini API over HTTPS. Your API key is encrypted on-device using the Android Keystore and is excluded from backups. Password fields and other sensitive inputs are never read, under any circumstance — see the README for the exact rules this app follows.
